subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: Tiergarten: Berlin's Green Heart
description: A fast breakdown of Tiergarten: Berlin's Green Heart for builders.

hook.text: Berlin's Tiergarten was a royal hunting ground in the 1500s. Today it's a 520-acre urban park for 4 million people.

buildup.text: During World War II, the park was destroyed — trees cut for fuel, ground cratered by bombs, soil exhausted.

discovery.text: Berliners replanted the entire park after the war. Every tree you see today was planted since 1949.

twist.text: The Berlin Wall cut through the park's edge for 28 years. Its reunification mirrored Germany's own.

climax.text: Today the Tiergarten absorbs 6,500 tons of CO2 yearly and hosts 200 bird species. The regrowth succeeded.

punchline.text: Bombed flat. Cut in half. Replanted entirely. Still green.

quiz.question: What happened to Berlin's Tiergarten during World War II?
options: It was converted into an airfield for military planes
Trees were cut for fuel and the ground was cratered by bombs
It was preserved as a neutral zone under international agreement
